Subject: Aurora Systems - Demo + procurement sync

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the call last week. We're excited to see Redwood Inference in action. To make the demo productive we'll need AE + SE, plus a short procurement run-through and a security checkpoint with our InfoSec lead (Kevin) — all internal stakeholders on our side. The ask from procurement: confirm billing/contact details and high-level commercial terms during the same session if possible.

Time constraints: our engineers in APAC are only available after 19:00 PDT (next-day morning JST/SGT), procurement prefers US afternoons, and InfoSec can do EU mornings. I'm attaching our current SOW and a security questionnaire — please review and propose a structured session that minimizes wasted time for our teams.

Attachments: Aurora_SOW_v0.2.pdf (pdf, 420KB); security_questionnaire_v3.xlsx (xlsx, 80KB)

Preferred starting window: week of June 5. We can do:
- Tue Jun 6: 16:00-18:00 UTC (US morning / EU late morning / APAC evening)
- Wed Jun 7: 08:00-10:00 UTC (EU morning / US very early / APAC late afternoon)

If none of those work, willing to consider a two-part approach.

Best,
Maria
Director, Platform Engineering
Aurora Systems

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Aurora Systems - Demo + procurement sync

Maria — thanks for the context and the attachments, received and skimmed. Good idea to keep this tightly structured. Proposed approach (to save everyone's time): a single 90-minute "tri-phase" session with clear handoffs rather than separate full calls. Draft agenda below — happy to revise based on your priorities.

Agenda (90 minutes):
1) 0–30 min: Product demo (AE + SE) — focus on latency, routing policies, and private deployment options (we'll keep demos to short, focused flows)
2) 30–55 min: Security & data residency Q&A with Kevin (SE + Security SME) — go through the questionnaire highlights and any blockers
3) 55–90 min: Procurement & commercial basics (AE + Sales Ops) — billing, contract cadence, and next steps (DocuSign link prep)

Why this helps: by aligning the security checkpoint in the middle we keep the technical dialog fresh for InfoSec and leave procurement to confirm decisions after technical alignment.

Availability for Redwood:
- Jun 6 16:00-17:30 UTC — Aditya (AE) available, Dylan (SE) available, Marissa (Sales Ops) available
- Jun 7 09:00-10:30 UTC — Aditya (AE) limited, Dylan (SE) available remotely (late night PDT), Marissa unavailable

If Jun 6 window works for Aurora we can lock it. I also created a quick calendar poll: https://cal.poll/aurora-tri-phase — can you mark preferred slots? I'll send a calendar invite and attach an .ics once confirmed.

Action items for Aurora before the call:
- Confirm which people from InfoSec will attend the 25-minute security block (Kevin included?)
- Confirm procurement attendee (email listed — procurement@aurora-sys.com?)
- Any specific compliance docs you'd like on the call (SOC2, encryption, KMS/HSM)?

I attached a stub invite (rdw-demo-invite.ics) and will loop in Sales Ops for DocuSign prep once we have date.

Thanks — Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Quick note from the SE side — I can lead the security/Q&A portion with Kevin if that helps. A couple of items I'll prep and highlight live:
- Short demo of routing policies and private VPC setup (10 min)
- KV cache/batching behavior and expected latency impact for your mixed workloads (10 min)
- Quantization and cost tradeoffs for steady-state throughput (5 min)

Availability check: I can do Jun 6 16:00-17:30 UTC (works well) and Jun 7 morning UTC (also possible but not ideal due to timezone churn). If Jun 6 is confirmed I’ll request a brief pre-demo sync (30 min) with Kevin the day before to walk through the security questionnaire gaps.

Also, if Aurora prefers an APAC-friendly recurring handoff cadence (rotating weekly window so each region occasionally sees the live demo), we can propose a follow-up short 30-min rotating slot for engineers to observe hands-on. That keeps the main decision-makers in a single consolidated session and opens a recurring, lighter-weight window for deep technical follow-ups.

Dylan
